text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition can't explain your outcome: you and the hired candidate are both women, so sex doesn't distinguish you. An all-women panel in economics is unusual, but unusual isn't evidence of bias against you specifically. Raising it would weaken your credibility and shift attention away from your actual strong point.

Your real grievance is substantive: on paper you out-qualify the appointee on degree completion, publications and teaching. That's a question about how "industry experience" was weighted, whether it appeared in the advertised criteria, and whether scoring was documented.

Press that instead. Send a written follow-up citing your original request and any statutory or policy deadline for reasons, and ask for the panel's scoring against published criteria.
